title: Signal · Sunday 15 November
overview: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia days before its results, Anthropic sets out its IPO as model prices fall, banks count AI use cases while Swiss banks lack scale, ChatGPT and Gemini reach for customers' wallets, and Crédit Agricole bids to reshape Italian banking.

top.headline: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia as Colette Kress takes charge before Tuesday's results
top.summary: Nvidia's board said on 12 November that Jensen Huang, co-founder and chief executive for 33 years, had resigned as president, CEO and director with immediate effect. Colette Kress, chief financial officer since 2013, is interim chief executive while the board looks for a successor. The board had opened an independent investigation on 8 November after reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
top.background: The shares fell 14 percent at the open and closed 4 percent lower, according to SRF. Huang has agreed to testify to Congress behind closed doors by Thanksgiving, TechCrunch reports.
top.why: Nvidia sits under most AI computing, and SRF's business desk suggests it may finance its chip customers less under Kress, which could slow the AI build-out.
top.watch_next: Results on 17 November, with Kress's written commentary, are the first test of the new leadership.

top.headline: Anthropic seeks up to USD 64 billion in its IPO as model prices fall
top.summary: Anthropic launched the roadshow for its IPO on 10 November: 825 million Class A shares at USD 70 to 78 each, to list on Nasdaq as ANT. The sale would raise USD 57.75 billion to 64.35 billion and value the company at up to USD 1.404 trillion, according to TechCrunch, which cites CNBC for trading close to 19 November. A day earlier Anthropic cut the price of its top models: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cost USD 8 per million input tokens and USD 40 per million output tokens.
top.background: Fable 5.1 cost USD 10 and USD 50. OpenAI's third-quarter revenue passed USD 10 billion for the first time, Bloomberg reported, according to TechCrunch.
top.why: Public markets will soon price frontier AI daily, and cheaper top models lower the cost of the agent work banks are piloting.

top.headline: Banks announce a record 111 AI uses; McKinsey sees Swiss banks lacking scale
top.summary: The 50 banks in the Evident AI Index announced 111 new AI use cases in the third quarter, a record, 22 of them agentic, yet only 21 percent disclosed an outcome. McKinsey's Global Banking Annual Review 2026 found Swiss banks more profitable and more highly valued than their peers, but behind large international groups in AI budgets and infrastructure, according to finews.
top.background: McKinsey surveyed about 46,000 customers in 13 countries, not including Switzerland: 74 percent of those using generative AI for money matters do so on platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, yet 62 percent would rather get such help from their own bank.
top.why: Swiss banks keep their clients' trust but lack the big groups' budgets, so showing value per use case will decide where their AI money goes.

top.headline: ChatGPT and Gemini reach for customers' cards and bank accounts
top.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on 13 November with American Express, Mastercard and Visa: its dots agents can buy for US Pro subscribers, each purchase approved by Face ID or fingerprint and paid with a tokenised card number, according to The Statesman and FinanceFeeds. The same day Google let all US Gemini app users connect Google Wallet, and bank and card accounts through Plaid, for read-only spending insights.
top.background: In a Dallas Fed survey of 70 bankers, 11.4 percent said their bank already restricts customers' AI agents online and 22.9 percent plan to within six months, according to PYMNTS.
top.why: AI labs are building the place where customers look at their money and decide to spend it, which pushes bank apps and card relationships further back.
top.watch_next: OpenAI says it wants to allow purchases approved in advance within spending limits, which would test banks' fraud and consent rules.

top.headline: Crédit Agricole bids to merge Banco BPM as UniCredit nears Commerzbank control
top.summary: Crédit Agricole proposed on 9 November to merge Banco BPM with Crédit Agricole Italia, creating Italy's third-largest banking group with 6.5 million customers and more than 2,300 branches. Banco BPM shareholders would get a 20 percent premium and a EUR 1 billion extraordinary dividend, and Crédit Agricole's stake would rise from 29.6 percent to about 45 percent. UniCredit, after a record EUR 3.3 billion quarter, expects the last approvals for a larger Commerzbank stake by the end of November, finews reports.
top.background: Metro Bank opened a formal sale process on 12 November, saying it was in no active talks with any bidder, Reuters reported.
top.why: Each deal brings years of system migration, and BaFin's fine over Deutsche Bank's Postbank move shows what a migration done badly costs.

items.headline: Wealth software reshuffles: FNZ retreats, Avaloq goes to the US, Volaris buys Allocare
items.summary: FNZ said on 12 November it will cut jobs and close offices in Singapore, the Nordics, Spain, Italy and France to focus on the UK, Australia, New Zealand and the US. Avaloq launched Avaloq Mosaic for US wealth managers on 10 November, and Lucerne's Allocare said it has belonged to Constellation's Volaris since 1 October.
items.why: Swiss private banks and independent managers using these vendors should check roadmaps and support commitments as owners refocus.

items.headline: Microsoft restores its services after a global outage that revived concentration-risk worries
items.summary: A cascading failure from 12 November took down Outlook, Teams, Copilot and Defender worldwide; Microsoft said only that a large number of servers had become unexpectedly unavailable, TechCrunch reports, and on Saturday morning that all services were back, according to SRF. Bern professor Matthias Stürmer called it a wake-up call and urged firms to find alternatives (translated from German).
items.why: Banks under FINMA's operational resilience rules and DORA must show they can run critical services through such an outage, Copilot included.

items.headline: Global banks fund a joint stablecoin as Coinbase wins its US trust charter
items.summary: Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Santander and Deutsche Bank are among banks committing about USD 270 million to fund five years of a joint dollar stablecoin issuer, Project Faro, Bloomberg reported according to Decrypt, which lists UBS among the participants. Coinbase won final OCC approval for its national trust company, and Morgan Stanley agreed to buy digital transfer agent Vinyl Equity.
items.why: Large banks are building their own token rails; Swiss banks weighing franc stablecoins or tokenised deposits now have a benchmark for cost and partners.

items.headline: Surveys find AI widespread in bank risk and investment work, with narrow uses
items.summary: A survey of 300 credit, treasury and risk leaders at banks in 31 countries by FT Longitude, SAS and Microsoft found 82 percent use generative AI and 41 percent agentic AI in decision-making. A Forrester study for BlackRock's Aladdin found 87 percent of investment firms have deployed AI or set up use cases, mostly for narrow tasks.
items.why: Adoption is wide yet shallow; budgets will follow the uses that measurably change a credit or investment decision.

items.headline: Bern Cantonal Bank will fold its IT subsidiary Aity back in from 2028
items.summary: BEKB said on 10 November that Aity, the IT subsidiary it founded in 2022, will be fully integrated into the bank on 1 January 2028, because the separate structure proved too complex and business with outside clients grew less than expected, finews reports.
items.why: A test case for Swiss banks weighing whether to run IT as a separate company that also sells to other banks.

items.headline: Finance ministry fines former Credit Suisse chair Urs Rohner over false information to FINMA
items.summary: The Federal Department of Finance fined Urs Rohner CHF 24,840 and gave him a suspended penalty of 144 daily rates of CHF 690 for knowingly giving FINMA false information about Credit Suisse's surveillance of staff, according to SRF Investigativ and Republik, as reported by finews. The order is not final; Rohner rejects the allegations and is going to court.
items.why: Board members' personal liability for answers to the supervisor becomes concrete while Parliament weighs FINMA's new powers.

items.headline: SNB sees no credit crunch as US ten-year yields pass 5 percent
items.summary: At its annual discussion with the Federal Council on 11 November, the SNB said lending kept growing after Credit Suisse's collapse, with no sign of a credit crunch, and confirmed growth forecasts of 1.5 to 2 percent this year and about 1.5 percent in 2027. US ten-year yields briefly rose above 5 percent as the Fed weighed a larger rise.
items.why: The SNB's finding will be cited in the UBS capital debate, where banks warn that higher requirements would curb lending.

items.headline: Swiss Life and Zurich grow premiums despite slower inflows and storm claims
items.summary: Swiss Life lifted premiums 8 percent to CHF 17.4 billion in the first nine months, while net new money in third-party asset management slowed, finews reports. Zurich grew property and casualty premiums 7 percent on a comparable basis to USD 42.1 billion, as storms in Switzerland, Germany and Italy raised claims.
items.why: Both enter 2027 planning with growing premiums, while storm costs keep claims handling and pricing high on their agendas.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen and opens Gemini 4 Carbon to all developers
items.summary: Google said on 12 November that Gemini 4 Hydrogen, built for everyday coding and agents, scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 50 for Gemini 4 Argon, at USD 1.50 per million input and USD 7.50 per million output tokens. Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model, opened to all paying developers on 10 November at USD 2 and USD 10.
items.why: Capable models keep getting cheaper across labs, which improves the cost case for agents on routine bank work each quarter.

items.headline: Databricks turns Genie into an autonomous agent and links it to ChatGPT and Claude
items.summary: Databricks said on 11 November that Genie now runs long tasks on its own within guardrails, drawing on Genie Ontology, while Unity Gateway lets administrators control tools, trace actions and cap spending. Plugins bring that context into ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot Cowork and Grok, and on 13 November it set out how OpenAI models work on governed Databricks data.
items.why: Banks that keep their data in Databricks can let staff use their chosen assistant without copying data out, with access rules carried along.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Architecture & TOM can show Genie Ontology and Unity Gateway as the governed context layer between a bank's data platform and its assistants.

items.headline: Anthropic lets companies run Claude Managed Agents on their own infrastructure
items.summary: Anthropic launched self-hosted Claude Managed Agents on 12 November: customers run the whole service on their own infrastructure and store agents, sessions and session history there, with model requests going to the provider they choose, Anthropic by default. Access is by request through Anthropic's account teams.
items.why: Keeping agent state in-house addresses a common data-residency question in Swiss and EU outsourcing reviews.
items.for_your_skills: For your skills: Regulatory Audit and Architecture & TOM can list self-hosted Managed Agents as a hosting option where client data must stay on the bank's own infrastructure.

items.headline: Breach at AI host Fireworks exposes some Notion AI chat transcripts
items.summary: Fireworks AI, which serves open models to developers, said attackers breached its cloud provider and reached a development system holding customers' billing information and some datasets, TechCrunch reports. Notion, one confirmed affected customer, said about 1 percent of its own customers were affected.
items.why: An AI vendor's own providers are part of a bank's third-party risk, so contracts should name them and set breach notice terms.

say_it_today: Banks announced a record 111 AI use cases last quarter, but only one in five came with a stated result; with the AI labs now asking public markets to price their own returns, boards will start asking banks for the same evidence.
thread: AI moved closer to the money this week. Anthropic asked public investors for up to USD 64 billion, Nvidia lost its founder and chief executive of 33 years, and OpenAI and Google put their assistants next to customers' cards and bank accounts. Banks answered with numbers, a record 111 new use cases in a quarter, but only one in five came with a stated result. Microsoft's outage, which began on 12 November and ended with all services restored on Saturday morning, showed how many firms now run on one supplier. The common thread is dependence: on a few providers, and on proof that the spending pays.
